author: Siobhan McAndrew
title: Floriston Fire burns 600 acres southwest of Reno, north of Lake Tahoe - NewsBreak
text:
By Siobhan McAndrew Jaedyn Young Brett McGinness ,
11 hours ago
This is a breaking news story that will be updated.
The Floriston Fire, first reported shortly after 10 a.m. Wednesday, has grown to 600 acres burned just east of the Nevada-California state line, about 11 miles north of Lake Tahoe and 19 miles southwest of Reno.
The fire was at 5% containment as of 7 p.m. Wednesday. Its cause is under investigation.
In total there are 20 engines, 10 water tenders, two helicopters, eight dozers and 12 handcrews fighting the Floriston Fire.
The fire has prompted evacuation orders and warnings on both sides of the state line, including in neighborhoods that had been evacuated for the Bug Fire and Hawk Fire last month.
Westbound Interstate 80 remains closed to all traffic.
Here’s what to know.
Air attack against Floriston Fire to continue overnight Night-flying helicopters will continue to fight the Floriston Fire Wednesday night into Thursday, according to the Truckee Meadows Fire Protection District .
"As the fire lays down for the night, #TMFR crews will continue fire suppression, working to strengthen containment and keep the fire from making additional movement," the agency posted on Facebook on Wednesday evening.
A pair of water-collecting CH-47D Chinook heavy-lift tandem-rotor helicopters were operating between the fire and Boca Reservoir, approximately three miles to the west, according to fire.ca.gov .
The National Weather Service predicts clear conditions and south winds 5 mph in the area overnight; lows will drop into the low to mid-40s.
Floriston Fire evacuation orders in Nevada County; warnings in Washoe, Sierra counties
The first evacuation orders are in place for the Floriston Fire in Nevada County, California near the Nevada-California state line.
Evacuate now orders were issued to residents of Zone NCO-E379-A in eastern Nevada County, which contains the communities of Floriston and Farad, shortly before 5 p.m. Wednesday.
Evacuation warnings are now in place for Sierra County Zones SIE-E099 and SIE-E100-B, an area on the south side of Sierra County between the Truckee River to the east and CA-270 to the west.
" Be ready to evacuate" warnings have been issued for communities along the Truckee River/I-80 corridor in Washoe County between the community of Mogul and the Nevada-California state line. The order also extends into wilderness areas south to Snowflower Mountain and the Nevada-California state line.
No announcements have been made for temporary shelters or animal evacuation centers in the area.
Evacuees can get discounted rates at Reno hotels:
J Resort is offering rates of $49 a night with no resorts fees at J Resort using the rate code Flor26 during online booking. Caesars Entertainment properties (aka "The Row") are offering rates of $59 a night at the Silver Legacy, Eldorado and Circus Circus Reno using the code SCLOC26 during online booking, or by calling 800-223-7277. The Grand Sierra Resort is offering rates of $59 with no resort fees, along with complimentary RV and trailer parking, using the code EVACUEE when booking online, or by calling 775-789-2000. Floriston Fire reduces air quality in northwestern Nevada Air quality in the area of the Floriston Fire improved to "moderate" as of 7 p.m. Wednesday.
Earlier on Wednesday afternoon, the Northern Nevada Public Health Air Quality Management Division issued an air quality alert for the Verdi area, with air quality registering at 109 — "unhealthy for sensitive groups." Residents are advised to avoid strenuous outdoor activities.
Particle pollution of 2.5 microns were the primary driver of the worsening air conditions.
Other parts of Northern Nevada stretching from the Black Rock Desert to the north and Hawthorne to the south have seen air quality diminish to "moderate."
Weather conditions near Floriston Fire: moderate temperatures, breezy The National Weather Service predicts mostly clear skies and southwest winds 5 to 10 mph overnight; clear, breezy conditions are expected to persist for the next several days.
Wednesday night: Areas of smoke. Mostly clear, with a low around 43. Southwest wind 5 to 10 mph. Thursday: Patchy smoke before 10am. Sunny, with a high near 67. Southwest wind 5 to 10 mph. Thursday night: Clear, with a low around 38. Southwest wind 5 to 10 mph becoming light in the evening. Friday: Sunny, with a high near 73. Light and variable wind becoming north 5 to 10 mph in the afternoon. Friday night: Clear, with a low around 43. North wind around 5 mph becoming calm in the evening. Saturday: Sunny, with a high near 78. Calm wind becoming east around 5 mph in the afternoon. Saturday night: Mostly clear, with a low around 46. Dry conditions have contributed to the spate of wildfires in northwestern Nevada and northeastern California over the past several weeks of summer. The central Sierra Nevada, site of the Floriston Fire, saw warmer-than-average conditions and a snowpack well below normal during the winter of 2025-26.
Area of Floriston Fire steep, heavily forested
The Floriston Fire is burning an area in a Sierra Nevada canyon that serves as a route for the Truckee River between Lake Tahoe and Reno, and for Interstate 80 between Reno-Sparks and the greater Sacramento area.
The rugged terrain is home to towering pines, with manzanita, bitterbrush and rabbitbrush understory fuels. The Bug, Stampede and Hawk fires, which burned areas of northwestern Nevada and northeastern California in August, were fueled mainly by tall grass, brush, pinyon and juniper.
The unincorporated community of Floriston, California, which was under evacuation orders Wednesday afternoon, has a population of about 80 residents.
This article originally appeared on Reno Gazette Journal: Floriston Fire burns 600 acres southwest of Reno, north of Lake Tahoe
